# Results — Study 96 (New-Year-Pop) on the real tapes

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The object is the **monthly
small-minus-large return spread**: each month, the small-cap index return minus the
large-cap index return. We ask whether **January's** spread is significantly higher than
the rest of the year (Keim 1983; Reinganum 1983), test the famous post-publication decay,
and run a seasonal timer (hold small in January, large the other eleven months, net of 10
bps/switch) against buy-and-hold of each leg. As-of **2026-06-13**; match the fingerprints
to confirm you hold the same tapes.*

## Data stamp

| Pair | Adjustment | Window | Months | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|--:|---|
| **^RUT vs ^GSPC** (long sample) | **price-only** (no dividends — Yahoo has none for these indices) | 1990-02 → 2026-05 | 436 | `4d6121368a41` |
| **IWM vs SPY** (tradable) | **total-return** (dividends folded in) | 2000-06 → 2026-05 | 312 | `05eb4d6d2811` |

> **Price-only is stated, not buried.** The long-sample spread omits the (small) dividend
> difference between small and large caps. For a *seasonal contrast within* the spread this
> is benign — the dividend gap is roughly constant across calendar months — but it is not a
> total-return number. The tradable IWM/SPY pair is total-return and carries the dividends.

## Is January's small-minus-large spread special? — no.

| Quantity | ^RUT vs ^GSPC (price-only, since 1990) | IWM vs SPY (total-return, since 2000) |
|---|--:|--:|
| January mean spread | **+0.19%/mo** | **+0.14%/mo** |
| Rest-of-year mean spread | +0.01%/mo | +0.07%/mo |
| **January-minus-rest contrast** | **+0.18 pts** | **+0.07 pts** |
| **HAC *t* on the contrast** | **+0.31** | **+0.12** |
| January small>large hit-rate | **16/36 (44%)** | **13/26 (50%)** |
| Wilson 95% interval on hit-rate | **[30%, 60%]** | **[32%, 68%]** |

Both HAC *t*-stats are nowhere near the **2** the desk requires; the January hit-rate is at
or below a coin and its Wilson interval straddles 50%. **The January effect is statistically
absent in the modern tape.**

## Did it decay after Keim/Reinganum (1983)? — can't test it here.

| Quantity | ^RUT vs ^GSPC |
|---|--:|
| January spread, pre-2000 (9 Januaries) | +0.03%/mo |
| January spread, 2000+ (27 Januaries) | +0.25%/mo |
| Decay (early − late) difference | **−0.22 pts** |
| Welch *t* on the difference | **−0.13** |

The decay test has **almost no power**: Yahoo's ^RUT history begins in 1990, so the
"pre-publication" era (the 1970s–early-1980s, when Keim and Reinganum measured the effect)
is *entirely outside our data*. On the 9 vs 27 Januaries we do have, the difference is
indistinguishable from zero (and the point estimate is, if anything, slightly *higher*
post-2000). We cannot certify decay on this tape; the honest reading is that the effect is
simply **absent throughout the post-1990 window** — consistent with a literature that dates
the strong decay to the mid-1980s, before our coverage starts. → 3rd axis **NOT SUPPORTED**.

## Could you trade it? — no edge over just holding large caps.

Seasonal timer (small in January, large otherwise), net of 10 bps/switch:

| Arm | CAGR (long) | Sharpe (long) | CAGR (tradable) | Sharpe (tradable) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Seasonal timer** | 8.93% | 0.640 | 8.38% | 0.593 |
| Small buy & hold | 8.45% | 0.517 | 8.60% | 0.514 |
| Large buy & hold | **9.02%** | **0.662** | 8.53% | **0.619** |

The timer's tiny CAGR edge over small-cap buy-and-hold comes from sitting in large caps 11
months a year — i.e. it is *mostly the large-cap index*. It does **not** beat simply holding
the large-cap index (9.02% vs 8.93% long; 0.619 vs 0.593 Sharpe tradable). There is no
tradable January-tilt edge. → Tradability **MIRAGE**.

## How to read it

- **Signal → NONE.** January's small-minus-large contrast is +0.18 pts (HAC *t* = +0.31)
  long, +0.07 pts (*t* = +0.12) tradable — pure noise on this bench. Hit-rate at/below a
  coin.
- **Tradability → MIRAGE.** The seasonal timer doesn't beat holding large caps, net of
  costs.
- **"Decayed since Keim/Reinganum?" → NOT SUPPORTED.** The strong era predates Yahoo's
  ^RUT coverage; on 1990+ data the effect is already gone, and the pre/post difference is a
  statistical zero with almost no power.

This is the *January seasonal in the size spread* — distinct from the unconditional size
premium (see [Study 44 — Growth-Spurt](../../44-growth-spurt/)) and from the
"as-January-goes-so-goes-the-year" barometer (see [Study 80 — Cold-Open](../../80-cold-open/)).

## Reproduce

```bash
python examples/verify.py              # real tapes (this doc)
python examples/run_synthetic_demo.py  # offline positive/negative control
```
